title: Sudden breathlessness
candidateBrief: You are a junior doctor in an urgent care centre. Emma Wilson, 32, presents with breathlessness that started this morning. Take a focused history. You may use the Examine and Investigations panels. You will be asked questions afterwards.

patient.name: Emma Wilson
patient.openingStatement: I just can't seem to get my breath since this morning, and there's a sharp pain on the right side when I breathe in.
patient.demeanour: Anxious, slightly breathless, pauses mid-sentence to breathe. Cooperative.
patient.speechStyle: Short sentences because of breathlessness. Everyday language.

ice.ideas: Wonders if she has a chest infection.
ice.concerns: Worried because it came on so suddenly.
ice.expectations: Hopes for antibiotics or an inhaler.

freelyShared: Breathlessness came on suddenly about four hours ago while getting dressed.
Sharp right-sided chest pain, worse on breathing in.

revealOnlyIfAsked.trigger: recent travel, long journeys or immobility
revealOnlyIfAsked.answer: I got back from a work trip to Singapore three days ago. Thirteen-hour flight.
Now you mention it, my left calf has been aching and it looks a bit puffy.
I'm on the combined pill. Nothing else.
I coughed up a little streak of blood this morning, which scared me.

revealOnlyIfAsked.trigger: fever, cough with phlegm, or feeling unwell before
revealOnlyIfAsked.answer: No fever, no colds. I felt completely fine until this morning.

revealOnlyIfAsked.trigger: previous clots, past medical history, family history of clots
revealOnlyIfAsked.answer: Never had anything like it. My mum had a clot in her leg after an operation.

revealOnlyIfAsked.trigger: possibility of pregnancy or last period
revealOnlyIfAsked.answer: My last period was two weeks ago. I don't think I'm pregnant.

patient.cue: I did have that really long flight, but that wouldn't matter, would it?

examFindings.finding: HR 112 regular, BP 118/76, RR 24, SpO2 93% on air, temperature 37.1°C.
Chest clear, equal air entry, no wheeze. Pleural rub not heard.
Left calf 3 cm larger than right, tender along deep veins, mild pitting oedema.
Tachycardic, heart sounds normal, JVP not raised.

investigations.result: Sinus tachycardia 112 bpm, no other changes.

postEncounterQuestions.q: What is the most likely diagnosis and which risk factors support it?
postEncounterQuestions.modelAnswer: Pulmonary embolism, probably from a left-leg DVT. Risk factors: recent long-haul flight, combined oral contraceptive pill, family history of VTE.

postEncounterQuestions.q: How would you investigate and manage her?
postEncounterQuestions.modelAnswer: Calculate Wells score (PE likely), give interim anticoagulation if no contraindication while arranging CTPA, oxygen to target saturations, analgesia, stop the combined pill, and plan ongoing anticoagulation for at least three months.

items.text: Characterises onset and severity of breathlessness
Asks about VTE risk factors: travel, immobility, surgery, contraception, previous or family history
Asks about leg pain or swelling
Explains the concern and next steps clearly
